title: Trial expiry is computed as trialStartedAt + plan.trialDays
description: subscription.service.js (~lines 459-485) sets trialStartedAt=now and accessExpiresAt=trialExpiresAt only when status==='trial' and plan.trialDays is set. Verifies the pure calculation in isolation from Stripe. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — the SubscriptionOrg model and its trialStartedAt/trialExpiresAt/accessExpiresAt fields were deleted entirely; trial state is now tracked via SubscriptionInstance.status='trial' and termStart/termEnd in the V2 entitlement ledger.
preconditions: A subscription-plan fixture with planType='trial' and trialDays=14
steps: Call the tier-subscribe function with status='trial' for an org and the 14-day trial plan
Inspect the returned SubscriptionOrg fields
expectedResult: trialStartedAt equals the call time, trialExpiresAt equals trialStartedAt + 14*86400000 ms, and accessExpiresAt equals trialExpiresAt exactly.

title: requireFeature() denies a request when the key is absent from req.entitlements.features
description: middleware/requireEntitlement.js requireFeature(key) checks req.entitlements.features.includes(key). This is the actual server-side enforcement that TierGate.jsx's client-side alert is only cosmetic for. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — requireFeature() was deleted entirely from middleware/requireEntitlement.js; replaced by requireEntitlement(key), which reads req.entitlements.entitlements and returns errorCode ENTITLEMENT_NOT_AVAILABLE, not FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE. See BILL-UNIT-009.
steps: Invoke requireFeature('vciso.advisor') as middleware on a mock request whose entitlements.features does not include 'vciso.advisor'
Inspect the response
expectedResult: Middleware short-circuits with 403 and body { success:false, errorCode:'FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE', message:'Feature "vciso.advisor" is not included in your plan.', details:{ feature:'vciso.advisor', tier } }; next() is not called.

title: requireFeature(key, {strict:true}) denies when entitlements have not resolved yet
description: Distinguishes the strict-mode failure (ENTITLEMENTS_UNAVAILABLE) from the normal feature-absent failure (FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE) so callers can tell 'plan doesn't have it' from 'we don't know yet'. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — requireFeature() and its strict:true option were deleted entirely; requireEntitlement() has no strict-mode equivalent and always fails closed (503 ENTITLEMENTS_UNAVAILABLE) when entitlements haven't resolved. See BILL-UNIT-010.
preconditions: req.entitlements is undefined/null (tierContext middleware did not run or failed)
steps: Invoke requireFeature('cloudPosture.multiCloud', { strict: true }) with req.entitlements unset
expectedResult: 403 { success:false, errorCode:'ENTITLEMENTS_UNAVAILABLE' }. With strict left at default (false), the same input instead fails open per the documented 'defaults to showing children' behavior mirrored server-side.

title: Over-cap comparison flags every usage dimension exceeding the target tier's limits
description: customer.controller.js downgrade over-cap logic compares current usage (users, projects, storageGB, cloudAssets, vendors) against the target tier's limits object and builds the details.overCap breakdown returned in the 422 OVER_CAP_NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED response. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — customer.controller.js's downgrade over-cap comparison logic was deleted entirely; customer.controller.js now exports only getPublicPlans, and the V2 downgrade request flow has no verified over-cap check. See BILL-INT-016.
testData: Current usage: users=12, projects=4, storageGB=80, cloudAssets=50, vendors=20. Target tier limits: users=10, projects=5, storageGB=100, cloudAssets=25, vendors=20.
steps: Call the over-cap comparison function with the current usage and target-tier limits above
expectedResult: Returned overCap object flags exactly 'users' (12>10) and 'cloudAssets' (50>25) as over-cap; 'projects', 'storageGB', and 'vendors' are not flagged since they are within or equal to the target limit.

title: requireModuleConfig() returns TIER_LOCKED when a per-module field is not enabled in plan.moduleDefaults
preconditions: Org's moduleConfig.auditAssurance.aiPlanGeneration = false (snapshotted from a lower tier's moduleDefaults)
steps: Invoke requireModuleConfig('auditAssurance', 'aiPlanGeneration') as middleware for this org
expectedResult: 403 { success:false, errorCode:'TIER_LOCKED', message:'Feature "aiPlanGeneration" is not available on your plan.' }.
description: Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — requireModuleConfig() was deleted entirely from middleware/requireEntitlement.js; the surviving exports are requireEntitlement and requireScanFrequency only.

title: A stripe_events record already marked status='processed' short-circuits re-processing of a duplicate webhook delivery
description: Stripe redelivers webhooks on timeout/ack failure; stripe.webhook.controller.js dedups via the stripe-event.model.js collection keyed by event.id before running any handler. Superseded by the 2026-08-04 billing rewrite — the Stripe integration, its webhook route, and the stripe_events collection were deleted entirely; no Stripe dependency remains anywhere in vibrantix-backend.
preconditions: A stripe_events document exists for event.id='evt_123' with status='processed'
steps: Re-deliver the same webhook payload (event.id='evt_123') to the dedup check
expectedResult: Handler for the event type is not invoked a second time; response is 200 { received:true, deduped:true }.

title: tierCode is accepted as free text and is not validated against the suggested enum on plan save
description: subscription-plan.model.js documents tierCode's suggested defaults (growth/scale/enterprise/trial/legacy_unlimited) explicitly as 'NOT enforced. tierCode is free text.' This is a real gap: a typo'd tierCode (e.g. 'entreprise') will save successfully and silently create an unreachable plan rather than failing validation.
steps: Create/save a SubscriptionPlan document with tierCode='entreprise' (misspelled) and scope='organization'
Reload the saved document
expectedResult: Current behavior: save succeeds with no validation error despite the misspelled tierCode not matching any of the conventional values — flagged as a data-integrity gap; recommend an enum or admin-side validation before this ships more tiers.

title: requireScanFrequency() rejects a scan frequency not permitted for the org's tier
preconditions: Org's resolved req.entitlements.entitlements['cloud.scan.allowed_frequencies'] = ['weekly','monthly'] (no 'hourly'), sourced from the V2 entitlement ledger, not the deleted plan.moduleDefaults.cloudPosture field
steps: Invoke requireScanFrequency() as middleware on a request whose body/query requests frequency='hourly'
description: middleware/requireEntitlement.js's requireScanFrequency() itself is unchanged post-rewrite, but its input source moved from the deleted plan.moduleDefaults.cloudPosture.allowedScanFrequencies to the entitlement key 'cloud.scan.allowed_frequencies' resolved onto req.entitlements.entitlements by the V2 composition/resolver pipeline.

title: requireEntitlement(key) denies a request when req.entitlements.entitlements[key] is not true
description: middleware/requireEntitlement.js requireEntitlement(key) reads req.entitlements.entitlements[key] and compares against the expected value (default true). This is the sole surviving server-side feature-gate middleware after requireFeature()/requireModuleConfig() were deleted in the 2026-08-04 rewrite.
preconditions: req.entitlements.entitlements resolved with 'module.vciso.enabled': false (or key absent)
steps: Invoke requireEntitlement('module.vciso.enabled') as middleware on a mock request whose req.entitlements.entitlements['module.vciso.enabled'] is false
Inspect the response
expectedResult: Middleware short-circuits with 403 { success:false, errorCode:'ENTITLEMENT_NOT_AVAILABLE', message:'Entitlement "module.vciso.enabled" is not enabled.', details:{ entitlement:'module.vciso.enabled' } }; next() is not called.

title: requireEntitlement() returns 503 ENTITLEMENTS_UNAVAILABLE (fail closed) when req.entitlements has not resolved, with no strict-mode opt-out
description: Unlike the deleted requireFeature(key, {strict:true}), requireEntitlement() has no strict-mode parameter — it always fails closed with 503 when req.entitlements.entitlements is falsy, whether or not entitlements resolution has genuinely failed upstream.
preconditions: req.entitlements is undefined/null on the request
steps: Invoke requireEntitlement('org.custom_roles.enabled') with req.entitlements unset
expectedResult: 503 { success:false, errorCode:'ENTITLEMENTS_UNAVAILABLE', message:'Subscription entitlements could not be resolved.' }. Confirms there is no equivalent to the old fail-open default behavior — the new middleware always denies when entitlements are unresolved.

title: requireEntitlement() bypasses the check entirely for req.userId==='service-account'; requireScanFrequency() has no matching bypass
description: middleware/requireEntitlement.js opens requireEntitlement's guard with `if (req.userId === 'service-account') return next();` to let internal microservice calls skip entitlement checks. requireScanFrequency() has no such bypass — verify this asymmetry and that the bypass cannot be triggered by an external/customer-facing JWT.
preconditions: A request authenticated via the internal service-account path (req.userId==='service-account')
A second request with a normal customer JWT that has somehow set req.userId to the literal string 'service-account'
steps: Invoke requireEntitlement('module.vciso.enabled') with req.userId==='service-account' and no req.entitlements at all
Confirm next() is called without inspecting entitlements
Invoke requireScanFrequency() under the same req.userId==='service-account' condition and confirm whether it also bypasses or still requires req.entitlements.entitlements
expectedResult: requireEntitlement() calls next() unconditionally when req.userId==='service-account', regardless of req.entitlements. requireScanFrequency() has no matching bypass in the current code and will still 503 ENTITLEMENT_NOT_CONFIGURED if entitlements are missing — confirm this asymmetry is intentional. req.userId itself must only ever be derivable from the verified internal auth path, never from a client-suppliable claim.

title: balance.service.reserve() rejects a reservation that would push usedValue+reservedValue over limitValue with 402 QUOTA_EXCEEDED
description: reserve() uses an atomic Mongo $expr guard ({ $lte: [{ $add: ['$usedValue','$reservedValue', amount] }, '$limitValue'] }) on the findOneAndUpdate filter so a race between two concurrent reservations can't both succeed past the limit.
preconditions: An EntitlementBalance row for entitlementKey='ai.credits' with limitValue=1000, usedValue=950, reservedValue=0
steps: Call balance.service.reserve() requesting 100 ai.credits with a fresh reservationId
expectedResult: Throws a QuotaExceededError (statusCode 402, errorCode 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED', details:{resource:'ai.credits', current:950, limit:1000}); reservedValue on the balance document is left unchanged at 0.

title: finishReservation('commit') cannot report actual usage greater than the original reservation amount
description: commit() rejects requestedActual > reservation.amount with 409 USAGE_EXCEEDS_RESERVATION, preventing a caller from reserving a small amount and then committing a larger one.
preconditions: A live 'reserve' EntitlementUsageEvent for reservationId='res-1', entitlementKey='ai.credits', amount=50
steps: Call balance.service.commit('res-1', { actual: { 'ai.credits': 75 } })
expectedResult: 409 error with errorCode 'USAGE_EXCEEDS_RESERVATION'; the balance's reservedValue/usedValue are left unchanged (the commit is fully rejected, not partially applied).

title: finishReservation('cancel') releases reservedValue back to zero without incrementing usedValue
preconditions: A live 'reserve' EntitlementUsageEvent for reservationId='res-2', entitlementKey='ai.credits', amount=200, with the balance's reservedValue=200
steps: Call balance.service.cancel('res-2')
expectedResult: Balance's reservedValue decreases by 200 back to 0; usedValue is unchanged (the amount applied to usedValue is forced to 0 for the cancel path). A new EntitlementUsageEvent with operation='cancel' and amount=200 (the original reservation amount, not 0) is recorded.

title: reserve()/commit()/cancel() are idempotent by reservationId — a replayed call never double-counts a balance
description: Each operation first checks for an existing EntitlementUsageEvent with the same reservationId+operation (or, for commit/cancel, any prior finalizing event) and returns { idempotent:true } without re-applying the balance mutation. Protects against duplicate retries from calling microservices (assistant-service, vciso-service, etc.) that don't get a clean response the first time.
preconditions: A completed reserve+commit pair already recorded for reservationId='res-3'
steps: Re-call balance.service.reserve() with the same reservationId='res-3' and the same items
Re-call balance.service.commit('res-3', ...) a second time
expectedResult: Both replayed calls return { reservationId:'res-3', ..., idempotent:true } and neither mutates usedValue/reservedValue a second time. Calling finishReservation('res-3','cancel') after it was already committed instead throws 409 RESERVATION_ALREADY_FINALIZED, since the two operations disagree.

title: Every DEFINITIONS entry with meterType term_quota or consumable gets resetPolicy='term'; every other meterType gets 'never'
description: entitlement-catalog.js derives resetPolicy purely from meterType via .map() at module load: ['term_quota','consumable'].includes(meterType) ? 'term' : 'never'. A future definition added with the wrong meterType would silently get the wrong reset behavior with no validation catching it at add-time (admin-catalog.controller.js's validateDefinition() checks meterType is a valid enum value but never cross-checks resetPolicy consistency).
steps: Load entitlement-catalog.js's DEFINITIONS export
Assert every entry with meterType in ['term_quota','consumable'] has resetPolicy==='term'
Assert every entry with any other meterType has resetPolicy==='never'
expectedResult: All DEFINITIONS entries satisfy the mapping with no exceptions. Flagged as a data-integrity gap: admin-created custom EntitlementDefinition rows via POST /api/admin/subscription-catalog/definitions set resetPolicy directly from the request body/default ('never') with no equivalent enforced coupling to meterType, so an admin could create a term_quota definition that never resets.
